signal.headline: Four VPN and firewall flaws joined CISA's exploited-vulnerabilities list between 29 October and 6 November
signal.summary: Between 29 October and 6 November 2026, CISA added flaws in Cisco's firewall software, Ivanti Connect Secure (two) and SonicWall's SSL VPN to its catalogue of vulnerabilities known to be exploited. The Cisco flaw can crash the device. The two Ivanti flaws can be chained: a file upload and a privilege escalation by an authenticated user. The SonicWall flaw can let a user with valid credentials for another sign-in method bypass SAML controls, including SAML-enforced MFA. CISA lists ransomware-campaign use as unknown for all four.

items.mapping_note: CISA lists ransomware use as unknown for these four. RETACH maps them to ransomware because a remote-access flaw has been used that way before (Unit 42 on CVE-2026-0257, covered in the 22 October Weekly Brief). The mapping is editorial.

intervention.name: Patch and exposure management for internet-facing remote-access and firewall devices
intervention.what: Keep a list of every VPN gateway and firewall that faces the internet, check each against the CISA catalogue, apply the vendor's fix or mitigation using CISA's due date as a benchmark, and restrict who can reach management interfaces.

expected_effect.direction: Expected direction: fewer known-exploited flaws left open on internet-facing devices, so fewer intrusions through that route.
expected_effect.label: Direction only, no sourced coefficient
